title: Range Sum Query - Mutable
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<int> tree: n+1 entries → O(n)
- vector<int> arr: n entries → O(n)
- int n: O(1)
- recursion: none
approach: Use a Binary Indexed Tree (Fenwick Tree) to support both point updates and range sum queries in O(log n) time. Each tree index i stores a partial sum covering a range whose length equals the lowest set bit of i. To update, propagate the delta to all covering indices; to query a prefix sum, accumulate all covering indices by stripping the lowest set bit. A range sum [left, right] is prefix(right) − prefix(left − 1).
hints: With up to 3·10^4 calls each to update and sumRange on a 3·10^4-element array, what total cost would result if every sumRange scanned its full range?

Use a Binary Indexed Tree (Fenwick Tree). For nums = [1, 3, 5], build a tree where tree[i] covers a power-of-two range; sumRange(0, 2) reads prefix(2) = 9 in O(log n) instead of scanning all elements.

build:
  for each i: add(i, nums[i])
add(i, delta):
  i += 1
  while i <= n: tree[i] += delta; i += i & -i
prefix(i):
  i += 1; s = 0
  while i > 0: s += tree[i]; i -= i & -i
sumRange(l, r) = prefix(r) − (l > 0 ? prefix(l−1) : 0)
update(i, val) = add(i, val − arr[i]); arr[i] = val

**Single element** - n=1, only index 0 exists
`Input: NumArray([7]), sumRange(0,0)` → `Expected: 7`
⚠️ Bug: prefix loop uses `for (i; i > 0; ...)` without incrementing i first → prefix(0) returns 0, sumRange returns 0

**Full range from 0** - left=0, right=n-1
`Input: NumArray([1,3,5]), sumRange(0,2)` → `Expected: 9`
⚠️ Bug: `prefix(right) - prefix(left)` instead of `prefix(right) - prefix(left-1)` → returns 8

**Update to same value** - delta is zero
`Input: NumArray([1,3,5]), update(1,3), sumRange(0,2)` → `Expected: 9`
⚠️ Bug: `add(index, val)` instead of `add(index, val - arr[index])` → returns 12

**Repeated updates** - same index updated twice
`Input: NumArray([1,3,5]), update(1,2), update(1,4), sumRange(0,2)` → `Expected: 10`
⚠️ Bug: not updating arr[index] after add → second update uses stale value 3, delta=1 instead of 2, returns 9

followUps.q: What if you need range updates (add v to every element in [l, r]) and point queries instead?
followUps.a: Store a BIT over the difference array. A range update [l, r] by v becomes add(l, v) and add(r+1, -v). A point query at i is just prefix(i). Time stays O(log n) per operation, space O(n).

followUps.q: What if the input is a 2D matrix with point updates and sub-rectangle sum queries?
followUps.a: Use a 2D BIT where each cell (r, c) covers a 2D range. Updates and queries each touch O(log R × log C) cells. Space becomes O(R × C).

followUps.q: What if indices arrive online with no known upper bound on n?
followUps.a: Use coordinate compression to map seen indices into a dense [1, m] range, then build a standard BIT of size m. Each operation is O(log m) where m is the number of distinct indices seen so far, and space is O(m).
